security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, environment variable examples, and ordinary ClickHouse schema terms. One semantic issue remains: the recommended bulk insert example teaches raw SQL string interpolation. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The recommended bulk insert example interpolates trade fields directly into SQL.
remediation.suggestion: Use ClickHouse client insert APIs or parameterized formats, and show escaping or validation for untrusted fields.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe SQL String Interpolation in Bulk Insert Example
semantic_findings.description: The recommended bulk insert example builds an INSERT statement by interpolating trade fields into SQL. If copied with untrusted input, it can cause SQL injection or malformed data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The markdown labels the bulk insert as efficient and interpolates string fields without escaping. It is documentation, not executed code, so impact depends on user adoption.

content.value_statement: ClickHouse projects often need better schema choices, faster queries, and safer ingestion patterns. This skill provides practical ClickHouse table, query, monitoring, and pipeline guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains MergeTree, ReplacingMergeTree, and AggregatingMergeTree table patterns.
Shows ClickHouse filtering, aggregation, window function, and time series query examples.
Covers materialized views for real-time rollups.
Lists monitoring queries for slow queries and table size checks.
Describes batch, streaming, ETL, and CDC ingestion patterns.
limitations: Does not connect to a ClickHouse server or execute queries.
Examples are generic and require validation against your schema and data volume.
Does not cover every ClickHouse engine or cloud deployment setting.
Some code examples need safer production handling before reuse.

use_cases.title: Design Analytics Tables
use_cases.description: Choose table engines, partitions, ordering keys, and data types for a new ClickHouse analytics workload.

use_cases.title: Tune Dashboard Queries
use_cases.description: Review slow analytical queries and identify filtering, aggregation, and monitoring improvements.

use_cases.title: Plan Data Ingestion
use_cases.description: Compare batch, streaming, ETL, and CDC patterns before moving operational data into ClickHouse.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Table Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClickHouse skill to compare MergeTree and ReplacingMergeTree for my events table. Explain when each fits.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Slow Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClickHouse skill to review this slow analytics query. Suggest ordering keys, filters, and aggregation changes. Keep assumptions explicit.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Rollup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClickHouse skill to design a materialized view for hourly metrics from an events table. Include source table requirements and query patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Pipeline Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClickHouse skill to plan a PostgreSQL to ClickHouse analytics pipeline. Cover batch loading, CDC, monitoring, and operational risks.

output_examples.input: My ClickHouse dashboard is slow when filtering by account and date.
output_examples.output: The response would review ordering keys, partition choices, filtered columns, slow query logs, and aggregation strategy.

output_examples.input: I need daily active users and retention metrics in ClickHouse.
output_examples.output: The response would outline a time-based schema, suitable aggregation functions, retention grouping, and materialized view options.

output_examples.input: We want to sync PostgreSQL changes into ClickHouse for reporting.
output_examples.output: The response would compare batch ETL and CDC, then identify monitoring needs, failure modes, and data validation checks.

best_practices: Validate every example against your ClickHouse version and schema before production use.
Batch inserts and align partitions with real query windows.
Review query logs and table statistics before changing keys or materialized views.
anti_patterns: Copying sample SQL without escaping user-controlled values.
Using many small inserts for high-volume event data.
Adding partitions, joins, or final reads without measuring performance impact.

faq.question: Does this skill execute ClickHouse queries?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use during analysis.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common ClickHouse engines and query patterns, but users should know basic SQL.

faq.question: Can it help design materialized views?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for real-time rollups and querying aggregated state tables.

faq.question: Does it provide complete database security hardening?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on analytics patterns and performance, not a full ClickHouse security review.

faq.question: What should I verify before using examples?
faq.answer: Verify your ClickHouse version, schema, data volume, access controls, and input sanitization needs.
